SkillGame · Wiring & Pin Map

A modern recreation of Bally's 1955 Skill‑Roll nickel‑flip game, run from a Windows mini‑PC over four FT232H USB boards. Flip the nickel side‑to‑side up the playfield; each hole it lands in scores and lights the reels.

4FT232H boards
28switches
26lamps
2solenoids
150NeoPixels
8+1playfield rows

The playfield

Every switch (S0–S27) and gobble hole (G1–G7) on the real glass. The nickel climbs row by row; land the top row to win, drop a gobble hole and it's over.

  1. Insert nickel → S0 Coin Up arms the game at level 1.
  2. Flip the levers to send the nickel side‑to‑side up the incline.
  3. Land a hole in the current row → adds its points, lights the tens & hundreds lamps, advances a level.
  4. Reach Row 8 (an 80‑pt hole) → Winner lamp + win‑lock solenoid.
  5. Gobble hole (S23) or Tilt (S27) → game over.
Switch input Tens lamp 10–90 Reel / indicator Solenoid NeoPixel SPI Not connected

The board & the signal flow

Each of the four devices is the same Adafruit FT232H breakout, told apart only by the FTDI serial number burned into it (GPIO1–GPIO4). In code, pins are addressed as D0–D7 = 0–7 and C0–C7 = 8–15.

Build notes

  • Board identity is the FTDI serial number, not the socket. Firmware matches each device by serial GPIO1…GPIO4, so the module burned GPIO1 must go in socket U1, GPIO2→U2, and so on — each socket's wiring assumes that map. Silk-screen the serial on each socket.
  • Inputs are active-High: 3.3 V rail, switch closes to the pin, 10 k pull-down to GND.
  • Lamps (16) switch through PN2222A transistors out to lamp harness J2; solenoids (coin/win lock) through TIP120 Darlingtons with 1N4004 flyback diodes.
  • NeoPixels: WS2812b strip (150 px, 5 V) driven from GPIO4 D1 / SPI MOSI at a 3 MHz clock.
  • Spare pins: D0/D2/D3 (MPSSE/SPI), C8/C9, and the 3V/5V header pins are unused on every board; GPIO4 C6/C7 are free.
